_readme: Recipes offered to the app under Recipes -> Recipe library. See RECIPES.md for the schema. Adding an entry here and pushing to main is all it takes: GitHub Pages redeploys and the phone sees it on the next open. An entry on a branch is not published until that branch reaches main.

recipes.name: Salt rolls
recipes.ingredients:
TANGZHONG
20g bread flour
50g whole milk
50g water

DOUGH
330g bread flour
7g instant yeast
35g sugar
6g fine sea salt
100g whole milk, lukewarm
1 egg + 1 yolk, room temperature
55g unsalted European butter, softened

PAN AND TOPPING
30g butter, melted, for the pan
30g butter, melted, for brushing after
Flaky Maldon salt
recipes.steps:
1. Tangzhong. Whisk flour, milk and water in a small pan over medium-low heat 2-3 min to a thick paste. Cool 5 min to lukewarm.

2. Dough. Combine flour, sugar, salt and yeast. Add milk, egg, yolk and the tangzhong. Mix low 2 min, then medium-low 5 min. Add butter a tablespoon at a time, then knead 8-10 min to the windowpane test.

3. First rise. Oiled bowl, covered. Use the Proof dough recipe: 80F at 60% humidity, about 60 min, until doubled.

4. Shape. Butter the pan with 30g melted butter. Divide into 9 pieces of 70-75g, roll each tight, arrange 3x3.

5. Second proof on the counter, covered, 45-60 min, while the oven and steel heat. Pull it slightly under-proofed - puffy, not fully doubled.

6. Bake. Send this recipe with the baking steel on rack 2. It soaks the steel for 45 min, then holds. Set the pan on the steel and press start on the oven.

7. Finish. Brush with the remaining 30g melted butter the moment they come out, scatter Maldon salt, rest 10 min in the pan.
recipes.notes:
2026-09-05 bake: good crumb, but the bottom was not crisp and the top was overcooked. Cause was the rear element - convection at 375F for 20+ min browns the crowns. This version drops it: bottom element only for the long middle, colour from a short top+bottom finish, and a preheated steel under the pan for the base.

Next time: check colour at the start of stage 4 and cut it short if they are already there. Target 195-200F internal (needs the probe).

recipes.name: Pork ragù over creamy polenta
recipes.ingredients:
PORK
3 pounds skinless, boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt), cut into 3 pieces
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon vegetable oil
1 large onion, finely chopped
6 garlic cloves, finely chopped
2 tablespoons tomato paste
½ cup full-bodied red wine
1 28-ounce can whole peeled tomatoes
4 sprigs thyme
2 sprigs rosemary
2 bay leaves

POLENTA AND ASSEMBLY
Kosher salt
1½ cups coarse polenta (not quick-cooking)
¼ cup unsalted butter
½ cup grated Parmesan (from about 2 ounces), plus more for serving
Freshly ground black pepper
½ cup chopped fresh parsley
Olive oil (for drizzling)
recipes.steps:
1. Season pork with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a large heavy pot over medium. Cook pork, turning often, until evenly browned, 10-12 minutes. Transfer to a platter and pour off pan drippings.

2. Wipe out any burned bits from pot, but leave the golden-brown pieces (doing this will keep the finished sauce from tasting bitter). Add onion and garlic to pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is starting to brown and caramelize, 12-15 minutes. Add tomato paste and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly darkened in color, 5-8 minutes.

3. Add wine and cook, scraping up any browned bits, until reduced by about half, 5-8 minutes.

4. Add tomatoes, crushing with your hands as you go, then add thyme, rosemary, and bay leaves; stir in 2 cups water. Add pork with any juices accumulated on the platter; season with salt and pepper.

5. Bring liquid to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, until pork is falling-apart tender, sauce is thickened (it will be thicker than a typical pasta sauce), and flavors have melded, 2-3 hours.

6. Using 2 forks, break up pork into pieces or shred it (your choice); taste and season with salt and pepper.

7. Pork can be cooked 5 days ahead. Let cool; cover and chill in sauce.

8. Bring 6 cups salted water to a boil in a large pot. Whisking constantly, gradually add polenta; reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, whisking often, until polenta is tender and creamy, 20-25 minutes (if polenta becomes too thick too soon, loosen mixture by adding more water and continue cooking). Add butter and ½ cup Parmesan to polenta and whisk until melted; season with salt and pepper.

9. Spoon polenta into bowls or onto a platter and top with pork. Scatter parsley and more Parmesan over top and drizzle with oil.
recipes.notes:
Marked “Excellent!!” on the printout.

Step 5 is the long one: 2½–3 hours simmering. The printed recipe says 2½–3; the timer here offers 3 so it does not go off early.

Nothing in this uses the oven — it is stovetop from start to finish.

recipes.name: Miso and soy Chilean sea bass
recipes.ingredients:
MARINADE
1/3 cup miso paste
1/3 cup sake
1/3 cup mirin
3 tablespoons soy sauce
1/4 cup packed brown sugar

FISH
4 (4 ounce) fillets fresh sea bass, about 1 inch thick
2 tablespoons chopped green onion
recipes.steps:
1. Whisk the sake, mirin, miso paste, brown sugar and soy sauce together in a bowl until the miso and the sugar have dissolved.

2. Put the fillets in a large resealable bag, pour the marinade over them, seal, and chill in the refrigerator 3 to 6 hours.

3. Lift the fillets out and discard the marinade. Pat them dry — a wet surface steams instead of glazing. Set them on a lined tray on rack 3.

4. Send this recipe. Stage 1 cooks the fish through at 300F with 30% steam, about 10 minutes. Stage 2 jumps to 482F on the top element alone for about 2-3 minutes to caramelise the glaze. Watch that second stage — brown sugar goes from lacquered to burnt quickly.

5. Scatter the green onion over the fillets and serve.
recipes.notes:
Converted from a broiler recipe: the original broils 6 inches from the element for 7-9 minutes with the oven door propped ajar. This oven has no broil, so it is split into a gentle steam bake to cook the fish through and a short top-element blast for colour. Splitting it also protects the glaze, which is a quarter cup of brown sugar and would scorch under 8 straight minutes of top heat.

Times are my estimates, not from the source — the source only gives the broiler timing. First cook: check at the end of stage 1 and treat stage 2 as the variable. Sea bass is done at about 130F internal; it will carry over a few degrees.

Rack 3 is a guess. If the glaze is not colouring in stage 2, move the tray a rack closer to the top element next time.

Stage 1 has no hold, so the oven preheats with the fish already inside. That gentle ramp suits fish, but it means the 10 minutes is time-at-temperature plus the ramp — expect the whole thing to run longer than 12.5 minutes on the clock.

recipes.name: Ultimate banana nut bread
recipes.ingredients:
565g bananas, 4 medium, ripe but not fully black (about 340g peeled)
115g plain Greek yogurt, preferably nonfat
2 large eggs, straight from the fridge
15g vanilla extract (1 tablespoon)
280g all-purpose flour
150g sugar, preferably toasted
85g oat flour, such as Bob's Red Mill
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 teaspoon baking soda
3g Diamond Crystal kosher salt (3/4 teaspoon; for table salt use half the volume)
3/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/2 teaspoon ground cloves
1/4 teaspoon ground or grated nutmeg
150g coconut oil, virgin or refined, creamy but firm, about 70F
170g toasted pecan or other nut pieces
Banana whipped cream, optional, to serve
recipes.steps:
1. Line a 10.5 x 5.5 inch loaf pan with a 9 x 13 inch sheet of parchment. Two 9 x 5 inch pans also work, lined with 7 x 13 inch sheets.

2. Peel the bananas and mash them with the Greek yogurt, eggs and vanilla in a medium bowl. If the bananas are underripe, cover the bowl and let the mixture stand 30 minutes.

3. Combine the flour, sugar, oat flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg and coconut oil in the bowl of a stand mixer with the paddle. Mix on low until the coconut oil disappears into a mealy powder.

4. Add the banana mash and mix only until the floury bits disappear. Fold in the nuts with a spatula, scrape into the pan and spread level. Set it on rack 2, low-middle.

5. Send this recipe. Stage 1 bakes 45 minutes at 350F on the top and bottom elements. Stage 2 drops the top element for the last 25 minutes so the centre finishes without the crown darkening further.

6. It is done when it is well risen and golden brown, and about 206F in the middle. Seventy minutes total is the recipe's own figure for a large loaf; two small loaves want about 45.

7. Wrapped tightly in foil it keeps 3 days at room temperature or a week in the fridge.
recipes.notes:
Stella Parks. The oat flour and the Greek yogurt are what keep the crumb moist, and the cinnamon-cloves-nutmeg blend is there to amplify the banana rather than to taste of spice. Do not drop them for a plainer loaf without expecting a different bread.

206F internal is the real doneness test and the probe is broken, so the 45/25 split is a stand-in for it. Check with an instant-read at the end of stage 2 before pulling it.

No rear element anywhere in this. Seventy minutes under convection would brown the crown long before the middle reached 206F -- the Salt rolls problem, over a much longer bake. Top and bottom for the first 45 is an ordinary home oven, which is what the recipe assumes; bottom only for the last 25 is the foil tent done with elements.

Bottom-element-only caps at 356F, so stage 2 has almost no headroom. Do not raise the temperature without turning the top element back on.

Vent opens on stage 2 to dry the surface. If the crust comes out tougher than you like, close it.

Rack 2 is my read of the recipe's 'lower-middle'. I still do not know which end of the 1-5 scale is the top, so check the first bake and correct this line.

Muffin variant from the source: divide the batter among 12 greased nonstick cups, about 120g each, and bake until domed and just browning at the edges, about 25 minutes. That is one stage, not two -- it is too short to need the split.
